paite: David in, "Jonathan ziak a hehpihna ka latsak theihna ding in Saul inkote lak a mi om lai a-om hia?" achi hi.
heading: David Leh Mephibosheth
english: David said, “Is there yet any who is left of Saul’s house, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”

paite: Saul inkote sikha khat amin Ziba a-om hi. David kiang a hoh ding in asam uhi. Kumpipa'n akiang ah, "Ziba na hi hia?" achi a; ama'n, "Na sikha amah ka hi," achi hi.
english: There was of Saul’s house a servant whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David; and the king said to him, “Are you Ziba?” He said, “I am your servant.”

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Pathian hehpihna ka latsak theihna ding in Saul inkote lak a mi om lai om lou uhia?" achi hi. Ziba in kumpipa kiang ah, "Jonathan in tapa khat anei lai a, amah khebai ahi," achi hi.
english: The king said, “Is there not yet any of Saul’s house, that I may show the kindness of God to him?” Ziba said to the king, “Jonathan still has a son, who is lame in his feet.”

paite: Kumpipa'n akiang ah, "Koi a om ahia?" achi hi. Ziba in kumpipa kiang ah, "Ngai in, Lo-debar ah Amiel tapa Makir inn ah a-om," achi hi.
english: The king said to him, “Where is he?” Ziba said to the king, “Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar.”

paite: Huchi in kumpipa David in mi asawl a, Lo-debar a pan Ammiel tapa Makir inn a pan mi ava pisak hi.
english: Then King David sent and brought him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo Debar.

paite: David kiang ah Saul tapa Jonathan tapa Mephibosheth ahong hi. Amai a lei si in zahtakna apia hi. David in, "Mephibosheth," achi a; ama'n, "En in, na sikha," chi in adawng hi.
english: Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, fell on his face, and showed respect. David said, “Mephibosheth?” He answered, “Behold, your servant!”

paite: David in akiang ah, “Lau ke'n. Na pa Jonathan ziak in hehpihna ka hon musak ngeingei ding. Na pu Saul gam tengteng ka hon pe nawn dia, ka dohkan ah an na ne gige ding," achi hi.
english: David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father. You will eat bread at my table continually.”

paite: Huchi in akun a, "Ui sisa bang lel na hon limsak, kei na sikha bang ka hi a?" achi hi.
english: He bowed down, and said, “What is your servant, that you should look at such a dead dog as I am?”

paite: Kumpipa'n Saul sikha Ziba asam a, akiang ah, "Saul thil neih tengteng leh a-inkote thil tengteng na pu tapa ka pe vek hi.
english: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said to him, “All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master’s son.

paite: Amah a ding in lei na lehsak dia, nang leh na tapate leh na sikhate teng in na pu tapa in nek ding aneihtheihna ding in na sepkhiakte na hon la ding. Na pu tapa Mephibosheth in bel ka dohkan ah an a-um gige ding," achi hi. Ziba in tapa sawm-le-nga leh sikha sawmnih anei hi.
english: Till the land for him—you, your sons, and your servants. Bring in the harvest, that your master’s son may have bread to eat; but Mephibosheth your master’s son will always eat bread at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

paite: Huchi in Ziba in kumpipa kiang ah, "Kumpipa ka toupa'n asikha thu apiak bang zel in na sikha in ahih ding," achi hi. Kumpipa'n, "Mephibosheth in ka dohkan ah kumpipa tapa bang in an a-um ding," achi hi.
english: Then Ziba said to the king, “According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so your servant will do.” So Mephibosheth ate at the king’s table like one of the king’s sons.

paite: Mephibosheth in tapa naupang anei a, amin Mika ahi. Ziba inn a om tengteng Mephibosheth sikhate ahi uh.
english: Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica. All who lived in Ziba’s house were servants to Mephibosheth.

paite: Huchi in kumpipa dohkan a an a-um gige ziak in Jerusalem ah Mephibosheth atengta hi; amah akhe lang tuak bai ahi.
english: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king’s table. He was lame in both his feet.
